title: Generational KV Lease Reclaimer: epoch-aligned probabilistic compaction and decode-aware backoff
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Paged attention KV stores accumulate small fragmented segments and short-lived hot slots that cause eviction churn during prefill/decoder phases. Current LRU-like eviction plus large pause compactions either (a) evict items still needed by in-flight decodes causing token recomputation and tail latency spikes, or (b) block GPU work during compaction leading to throughput regressions.

Proposal: Implement a generational "lease" system plus epoch-aligned probabilistic compaction that cooperates with the decode scheduler. Each KV fragment carries a compact lease header (generation id, last-touch epoch, compactability score). A low-overhead probabilistic sampler picks candidate fragments to coalesce in background windows detected via GPU idle signals and workload-safe epochs. The reclaimer prefers moving cold fragments into consolidated slabs rather than evicting them outright, and applies decode-aware backoff by respecting active decode reservations and by shrinking compaction batches when prefill pressure goes high.

Goals: reduce eviction-induced recompute, lower 95/99 tail prefill latency, and reduce long-term fragmentation without heavy synchronous GC pauses.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-tail prefill latency reduced by >=30% in mixed-sequence benchmarks (short+long) compared to baseline.
Eviction-induced token recomputation events reduced by >=40% in stress tests.
Background compaction CPU/GPU overhead <3% of steady-state serving CPU/GPU utilization under typical traffic.
No throughput regressions for <=128 token sequences (within +/-3% of baseline).
Feature gated behind runtime-flag and can be disabled without state loss; rollout plan validated on canary nodes.
Automated unit + integration tests + perf benchmarks in CI and nightly harness.
Conservative memory-safety checks and snapshot rollback implemented for first rollout.
design_notes:
Architecture summary:
1) Lease metadata: 16B header per fragment storing generation (2 bits), last_touch_epoch (24 bits), compactability_score (8 bits) and a small checksum. The header is packed to keep overhead minimal.

2) Generations: three classes (young, resident, cold). On touch, fragment moves to younger generation and lease TTL resets. Cold fragments are candidates for consolidation instead of eviction.

3) Probabilistic sampler: a lightweight reservoir-like sampler walks shard-level fragment lists during idle probes, computing a compactability priority = alpha*age + beta*fragmentation_penalty + gamma*(1 - recent_touch_weight). We tune alpha/beta/gamma offline per workload. Sampling avoids centralized locks using per-worker local queues and occasional merging.

4) Epoch-aligned compaction windows: instead of arbitrary background jobs we align compaction to logical epochs coordinated with the prefill/decoder scheduler. During low prefill epochs (detected by moving-average of outstanding KV prefill requests and probe of GPU SM occupancy), compaction kernels run, performing mostly in-place micro-moves or small bulk copy with attention-aligned memory layout to avoid reshuffling KV ranges needed by active decoders.

5) Decode-aware backoff: the scheduler exposes a hint API for decoders to declare in-flight KV ranges with soft reservations. Reclaimer will avoid candidates touching reserved ranges; when reservation high, compaction reduces batch size or pauses. We use a conservative policy to prefer compaction targets from tenants with low active sessions.

6) Kernel selection: two kernels implemented and chosen by the runtime per compaction task: (a) micro-move kernel (low-latency, few-block copy) for small fragments, (b) bulk-move kernel (coalesced, vectorized) for larger fragments. Kernel selector factors in fragment size, target alignment for attention access patterns, and current SM occupancy.

7) Safety: compaction is snapshot-based at fragment-range granularity with atomic rename of fragment descriptors; rollback available if decode failure observed. Metrics track bytes moved, items consolidated, and compaction time per shard.

8) Telemetry: expose compaction_candidates, compaction_success_rate, compaction_bytes_moved, eviction_count_pre/post, recompute_events, and per-tenant compaction_throttle metrics to console and per-route dashboard.
decisions: Use 3 generations (young/resident/cold) to balance metadata cost and reclamation granularity.
Adopt probabilistic sampling over global LRU to reduce lock contention and improve locality-aware picks.
Run compaction only during epoch windows when prefill pressure and GPU occupancy both indicate low risk.
Expose a soft reservation API from decoder scheduler rather than hard pinning to avoid deadlocks.
Implement two compaction kernels and let runtime pick based on fragment size and occupancy.
Keep lease header compact (<=16 bytes) to avoid amplifying memory pressure.
Feature will be feature-flagged and off by default for Dedicated/Private until thorough canarying.
Telemetry and budget-based throttles required before external rollout.
No immediate changes to persisted on-disk format; headers stored in memory-only metadata for v1.
Do not modify existing eviction quotas for first rollout; compaction acts as a non-intrusive background option.
Use conservative default tunables to prioritize stability over max compaction aggressiveness.
Implement per-tenant minimum residency to avoid compaction of low-volume but latency-sensitive tenants.
Prefer local shard compaction to cross-shard merges in v1 to reduce lock domains.
Avoid cross-GPU compaction moves in v1; all moves are intra-device.
Metric-backed rollback triggers: if recompute_events increase by >15% during canary, immediately halt and revert.
Support for replaying compacted fragments via existing state checkpoints to ensure crash recovery.
Use runtime-1.20 release as first supported platform; earlier runtimes unsupported due to kernel primitives.
Security review not required for v1 since no new exfiltration surface exposed; revisit for on-prem HSM integrations.
Prefer sampling windows every 500ms with adaptive backoff to avoid tight loops under pressure.
Document APIs in design doc and add integration tests in the paging harness.
Schedule cross-team review with Storage and Scheduler teams before merging main changes.
Limit maximum bytes moved per shard per epoch to configurable cap (default 64MB) to bound interference.
Telemetry events should include sample seed to aid reproducibility of compaction decisions.
Implement per-tenant and per-route opt-out flags to let customers disable compaction if desired.
Make the probabilistic sampler deterministic under a fixed seed for test harness reproducibility.
Keep compaction idempotent and replay-safe across restarts.
Do not perform compaction if any decoder reservation for the candidate shard is older than the current epoch threshold.
Ensure compaction path respects encryption-in-memory (keys remain unaffected); coordinate with crypto team if metadata layout changes.
Add GC safety net: if we detect runaway fragmentation growth, revert to simple eviction policy until debugging completed.
Use feature-flag rollout in console with two knobs: global_enable and aggressive_mode (default false).

tests_and_metrics: Unit tests for lease header encoding/decoding and sampler determinism.
Integration tests: simulate mixed tenant workload with bursty prefill to validate no recompute regressions.
Perf bench: 1k clients, mixed seq lengths, compare baseline vs feature on CPU/GPU.
Canary telemetry: compaction_bytes_moved, compaction_time_ms_p95, recompute_events, eviction_count, prefill_tail_ms.
Nightly regression: track 95/99 tail prefill latency and recompute_events over last 7 days.
Dashboard: per-shard breakdown plus tenant-level aggregate; alert if recompute_events increase by >15%.
CI: run deterministic sampler seed tests to ensure reproducible picks in test harness.
Stress test: long-running fragmentation grow simulation to ensure compaction keeps fragmentation slope negative.
Safety test: forced kernel failure during compaction to validate rollback path.
Performance budget: keep compaction overhead <3% measured as additional GPU time on compacting nodes.
Compare per-tenant cost impact and token compute amortization after compaction over 24h windows.
Measure memory delta post-compaction and validate it reduces active fragment count by target factor.
Capture logs for reproducing compaction decisions (seed, sampled ids, scores).
Add fuzz tests for lease header corruption and checksum detection.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Compaction interferes with latency-sensitive decodes -> Mitigation: decode reservation hints, conservative default tuning, and immediate rollback triggers.
Risk: Metadata overhead increases memory pressure -> Mitigation: 16B compact header, optional enable per-tenant, and cap on bytes moved.
Risk: Determinism differences between dev and prod sampling -> Mitigation: deterministic seed in test harness and extensive sampling unit tests.
Risk: Kernel regressions cause SM occupancy spikes -> Mitigation: gradual kernel rollout, microbenchmarks, and per-kernel telemetry.
Risk: Cross-team coordination delays -> Mitigation: schedule early review and provide minimal invasive v1 approach.
Risk: On-prem customers require explicit opt-out -> Mitigation: provide per-tenant opt-out and feature flag in Private packaging.
Risk: Compaction causes temporary increase in memory footprint during copy -> Mitigation: cap in-flight bytes per shard and prefer in-place micro-moves where possible.
Risk: Snapshot rollback complexity -> Mitigation: keep snapshot scope small (fragment-range) and add automated rollback tests.
Risk: Unexpected increase in recompute events -> Mitigation: telemetry + automatic halt and notify engineers.
Risk: Scheduler deadlocks with hard pinning -> Mitigation: use soft reservations and timeouts.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Merge behind feature flag to main with e2e tests disabled until canary clamp passes.
Stage 1: Internal canary on 5% of runtime-1.20 fleet with no external tenants; monitor recompute_events, prefill_tail_ms for 48h.
Stage 2: Enable for internal tenant workloads and low-risk customers (opt-in) with telemetry collection and manual kill-switch.
Stage 3: Expand to 25% of nodes, enable aggressive_mode=false, run 7-day stability window and performance comparisons.
Stage 4: Enable broader rollout and optional aggressive_mode for customers that opt-in to compaction cost optimizations.
Stage 5: Post-rollout: continuous tuning based on nightly harness; add release notes and migration guide for Dedicated/Private.
Rollback criteria: recompute_events > +15% for 2 consecutive hours OR prefill_tail_ms regression > +20% sustained for 30 minutes.
Support: runbook created and linked in comment; on-call notified during canary windows.
Telemetry: add compaction run traces to console traces view for quick triage.
Docs: public-facing PRD and internal engineering RFC linked for customer-facing questions.
